name: GA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+36 partisan lean makes a Republican win nearly impossible
Incumbent Nikema Williams is running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Williams at roughly 98% to win
model.rationale: GA-05's D+36 lean and Williams's incumbency and fundraising advantage leave the Republican challenger with no visible path; markets price her near certain to win. The forecast stays at a wide Democratic margin with modest uncertainty.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing the challenger within single digits would be the only signal worth revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Atlanta-based GA-05 is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+36. Incumbent Nikema Williams is running for another term after easily securing renomination, and she has raised about $600,000 for the race. Her Republican opponent, John Oscar Salvesen, reports no fundraising and has drawn no outside spending or expert attention.

With no public polls of the general election, the outlook rests on fundamentals: the district's overwhelming lean, Williams's incumbency, and her clear financial edge. Prediction markets price Williams at roughly a 98% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main question being the size of her victory margin rather than who wins.
